title: Given a string, count how many of its contiguous substrings are palindromes, counting each position separately even if the content repeats. Explain the Palindromic Subsequence DP pattern applied to counting, the recurrence, the complexity, and a banking use case.
shortTitle: Count of Palindromic Substrings (Total Number of Contiguous Palindromes)

s1_definition.profdef: The Count of Palindromic Substrings is a counting variant of the Palindromic Subsequence pattern. We decide for every contiguous range whether it is a palindrome using the ends-match-and-inner-is-palindrome rule, and we increment a running total each time a range is a palindrome. This yields a quadratic time and space dynamic program.

Rajesh and Priya each receive identifiers, and the bank totals all the palindromic fragments.

s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** The Count of Palindromic Substrings is a counting variant of the Palindromic Subsequence pattern. We decide for every contiguous range whether it is a palindrome using the ends-match-and-inner-is-palindrome rule, and we increment a running total each time a range is a palindrome. This yields a quadratic time and space dynamic program.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** The National Bank of India measures how much symmetric structure a batch file identifier contains by counting every symmetric fragment inside it, because many overlapping symmetric fragments suggest a machine-generated identifier. Rajesh and Priya each receive identifiers, and the bank totals all the palindromic fragments.

**One line to remember:** For every range, if its ends match and the inner range is a palindrome, count it and mark it a palindrome.

sections.s2_technical:
We reuse the boolean palindrome table where an entry for range i to j is true when that substring is a palindrome, and we keep a counter. Each time a range turns out to be a palindrome we add one to the counter. The recurrence is identical to the substring problem: a range is a palindrome when the end characters match and either the range is short, meaning length one or two, or the strictly inner range is already a palindrome.

Bottom-up: `int count = 0; for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) { dp[i][i] = true; count++; for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) { if (s.charAt(i) == s.charAt(j) && (j - i < 2 || dp[i+1][j-1])) { dp[i][j] = true; count++; } } }`. A concrete check: a string of three identical characters has six palindromic substrings, the three singles, the two adjacent pairs, and the whole triple. Senior nuance: this is quadratic in time and space, every single character already contributes one palindrome, and the expand-around-center variant counts in quadratic time with constant space.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — The National Bank of India wants a symmetry score for each batch file identifier, defined as the total number of symmetric fragments inside the identifier, because a high count of overlapping symmetric fragments is a strong hint that the identifier was machine generated rather than human assigned. Counting fragments naively is cubic. This is exactly how the Count of Palindromic Substrings works: it totals all contiguous palindromes in quadratic time with the standard palindrome recurrence.

The code defines a `BatchIdService` exposing `symmetryScore(identifier)` returning the count of palindromic substrings. A `Demo` runs it over a sample identifier and logs the score.

sections.s5_journey:
The input is the identifier AAA. We want the total number of contiguous palindromic substrings.

Step 1 — We seed the diagonal. The three single characters at positions zero, one and two are each a palindrome, so the count becomes three.

Step 2 — We check adjacent pairs. The pair at positions zero and one is AA with matching ends and a length under two, so it is a palindrome and the count becomes four. The pair at positions one and two is also AA, so the count becomes five.

Step 3 — We check the length three range. The ends at positions zero and two are both A and match, and the inner range at position one is already a palindrome, so the whole AAA is a palindrome and the count becomes six.

Step 4 — There are no longer ranges, so the final count is six, matching the three singles, two pairs, and one triple.

Step 5 — The method returns six. The output is below.

```
Oct 27, 2026 9:09:33 PM com.bank.batchid.service.BatchIdService symmetryScore
INFO: Symmetry score of AAA = 6
Oct 27, 2026 9:09:33 PM com.bank.batchid.BatchIdApplication main
INFO: Symmetry score for identifier AAA is 6
```

```
    │ len 3: AAA ends A==A, inner true → count=6

```

sections.s6_takeaway:
The Count of Palindromic Substrings is a counting member of the Palindromic Subsequence pattern, and it reuses the same decision I make for the longest palindromic substring, namely that a contiguous range is a palindrome when its two ends match and the strictly inner range is already a palindrome. The only addition is a running counter that I increment every single time a range turns out to be a palindrome, so overlapping and repeated palindromes are all counted separately.

I fill the boolean table by increasing range length so each inner decision is ready before the outer range needs it, and the total accumulates as I go, which keeps the whole thing in quadratic time and space. I point out that every single character already contributes one palindrome, so the count always starts at least at the string length, and that an expand-around-center approach counts in the same time with constant extra space.

At the National Bank of India I used this to compute a symmetry score for batch file identifiers, defined as the total number of symmetric fragments inside each identifier, because a high count of overlapping symmetric fragments strongly suggested a machine-generated identifier rather than a human-assigned one. I ran the counting dynamic program and returned the total. Walking through the shared palindrome recurrence, the per-range counting, and the fact that singles alone guarantee a baseline count is what convinces an interviewer I understand the counting form of the Palindromic Subsequence pattern.
